119-hjres-1.t: Proposes an amendment to the U.S. Constitution that would fix the size of the Supreme Court at nine justices: one Chief Justice and eight Associate Justices.

119-hr-1013.t: Lets retirement plans for public school, charity and church employees (called 403(b) plans) put money into pooled investment funds run by banks or trust companies, and into insurance company investment accounts. These plans are not allowed to use those options today.

119-hr-1181.t: Bars credit and debit card networks from using a separate merchant category code for gun stores, so those stores would be coded the same as general stores or sporting goods stores. The Department of Justice would enforce this and report each year on cases it brings.

119-hr-139.t: Makes daylight saving time permanent, so clocks would no longer change twice a year. States that do not observe daylight saving time now could pick the standard time for those areas.

119-hr-1689.t: Tells the Department of Homeland Security to grant Haiti "temporary protected status" for 18 months starting August 3, 2025. That status lets eligible Haitians in the U.S. work legally, protects them from being detained over their immigration status, and protects them from being removed while they hold it.

119-hr-2102.t: Lets veterans with a disability from combat receive their full military retirement pay and their disability compensation at the same time, including veterans with fewer than 20 years of service. Today, their retirement pay is reduced when they receive both.

119-hr-2140.t: Renews through fiscal year 2029 an Environmental Protection Agency program that gives grants, rebates and loans for replacing old diesel engines or adding pollution controls to them.

119-hr-2262.t: Changes the federal wage and hours law so that optional training outside an employee's normal working hours does not count as paid working time. This applies even if the employer offers the training, as long as skipping it does not hurt the employee's working conditions and the employee does no work for the employer during it.

119-hr-2965.t: Requires the Small Business Administration's yearly "small business regulatory budget" to be no more than zero. That budget is the cost a federal rule places on small businesses, whether from a new rule or from changing or repealing an old one.

119-hr-3276.t: Writes into law the Urban Bird Treaty Program of the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, which works with cities and towns to protect birds that live in or migrate through urban areas. It includes grants, through the National Fish and Wildlife Foundation, to government agencies, community groups and universities.

119-hr-3383.t: Lets closed-end funds (investment funds with a fixed number of shares traded on an exchange) put more of their money into private investment funds. It bars the Securities and Exchange Commission from limiting the sale or listing of these funds' shares, and it covers certain business development companies too.

119-hr-3898.t: Narrows which waters the Clean Water Act covers by excluding five things from the definition of "navigable waters": waste treatment systems, streams and ditches that flow only after rain, former wetlands now used as cropland, groundwater, and anything else the Army Corps of Engineers decides to exclude.

119-hr-4638.t: Makes a non-citizen who is convicted of, or admits to, harming an animal used in law enforcement (such as a police dog) ineligible to enter the U.S. and subject to deportation.

119-hr-5362.t: Names the Department of Veterans Affairs clinic in Marietta, Georgia, the Colonel Michael H. Boyce Department of Veterans Affairs Multispecialty Clinic.

119-hr-5763.t: Eases the financing rules for certain Small Business Administration loans used to buy, build or expand a business's property, including land. For loans on special-purpose or single-purpose properties, the borrower would have to put in 5% less of the total cost.

119-hr-5764.t: Requires Small Business Development Centers to help small businesses evaluate artificial intelligence, including by sharing best practices and guidance on using AI to plan for unexpected events.

119-hr-6398.t: Removes a Clean Air Act requirement that the Environmental Protection Agency review and comment on major federal projects and proposed federal rules that already go through a separate environmental review under another law (the National Environmental Policy Act).

119-hr-6472.t: Requires public colleges and universities that take part in federal student aid to charge in-state tuition and fees to students who live in Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands, American Samoa or the U.S. Virgin Islands and are U.S. nationals.

119-hr-6945.t: Lets states use money from the Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) program on pregnancy centers that support protecting the life of the mother and the unborn child. Those centers must also offer help to parents and families, such as relationship counseling, pregnancy and prenatal education, pregnancy tests, diapers, baby clothes and other material support.

119-hr-7567.t: The farm bill. It renews and changes Department of Agriculture programs through 2031, covering crop support payments, conservation, food assistance, farm loans, rural development, crop insurance, research, forestry, and foreign ownership of U.S. farmland.

119-hr-9436.t: Pushes back the deadline for new federal rules meant to protect North Atlantic right whales (an endangered species) from getting tangled in lobster and crab fishing gear. The deadline moves from 2028 to 2035. The rules must still require use of existing and new gear technology that lowers the risk to whales.

119-hr-9576.t: Writes into law the National Fraud Enforcement Division at the Department of Justice, which investigates and prosecutes fraud against taxpayer money and taxpayer-funded programs. The Justice Department created the division in April 2026.

119-hr-980.t: Removes the rule that the Department of Veterans Affairs' on-campus education and career counseling for veterans must be provided by VA counselors.

119-s-1003.t: Directs the Federal Communications Commission to issue an order explicitly allowing wireless emergency alerts to be sent to phones when there is a shark attack. Officials can already send these alerts for emergencies such as severe weather and missing children.

119-s-2393.t: Authorizes the Department of Veterans Affairs to carry out a major medical facility project in St. Louis, Missouri, in fiscal year 2026, and sets the most that can be spent on it. The project includes a new bed tower, an expanded clinical building, a combined administrative building and warehouse, a utility plant and parking garages.

119-s-254.t: Stops states from banning the sale, trade, transfer or possession of marine mammal ivory, bone or baleen that an Alaska Native legally made into authentic handicrafts or clothing.

119-s-284.t: Renews through fiscal year 2028 the board that runs the Congressional Award Program, which recognizes young people for service, initiative and achievement. The renewal counts as if it took effect October 1, 2023. The bill also drops the rule that the program's medals be made of gold-plated or rhodium-plated bronze, or bronze.

119-s-32.t: Adds two places where federal courts must hold sessions: College Station, Texas (Southern District of Texas) and El Centro, California (Southern District of California).

119-sjres-77.t: Ends the national emergency that President Trump declared on February 1, 2025, which was the basis for an extra 25% tariff on most imports from Canada (and an extra 10% on Canadian energy).

119-sjres-88.t: Ends the national emergency that President Trump declared on April 2, 2025, which was the basis for a 10% tariff on most imports and extra duties on certain trading partners.
